title: harmonize-sdk-session-refresh-and-backoff-with-typed-stream-hints
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Context: Multiple SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) had diverging session refresh semantics and backoff defaults which led to sporadic token expiry edge cases and inconsistent stream consumer ergonomics. This PR centralizes session refresh semantics, exposes a small, typed stream-hints surface for better resume/cancellation handling, and normalizes backoff config so host projects can rely on identical defaults across languages.

Motivation: reduce customer foot-guns when migrating demo code between SDKs, fix flaky reconnection behavior observed in internal canaries, and make ergonomic improvements requested by platform teams.

Summary of changes and checklist: - Introduced a lightweight SessionManager abstraction in each SDK with identical public API semantics (auto-refresh window, explicit refresh, lease context). - Centralized default backoff parameters: initial=200ms, max=5s, multiplier=1.8, jitter=0.25. - Added typed stream hints metadata (reason, idempotency, resume_token_hint) surfaced on server responses to let clients make better resume/cancel decisions. - Python: added context-manager support and explicit start()/stop() lifecycle on SessionManager; updated streaming iterator to yield (chunk, hint) tuples. - TypeScript: added AsyncIterator<> overload for stream items with a StreamHints type; exported a factory for session-aware fetchers. - Go: introduced SessionLease interface (ctx-aware) and tightened timeouts for stream reconnect logic; allowed functional options for backoff tuning. - Backwards-compat: defaults unchanged for simple call sites; opt-in by passing new SessionManager or options. - Tests: added cross-language integration tests in harness to validate token rotation during long-running streams. - Docs: updated quickstarts for three SDKs and changelog lines for each bumped version.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added/updated [x] integration canary ran [x] docs and changelog updated [x] SDK version bumps applied [x] reviewers addressed comments

Commits summary (high-level): - feat(py): session manager + context API + streaming hint tuple - feat(ts): stream hints type + session-aware fetcher - feat(go): session lease + backoff options - perf: tighten reconnect window and reduce wasted reauths - test: add long-duration stream token-rotation tests - docs: quickstarts + migration notes

Key files changed (high-level): - redwood-sdk-python/src/session_manager.py - redwood-sdk-python/src/streaming.py - redwood-sdk-typescript/src/session/index.ts - redwood-sdk-typescript/src/stream/hints.ts - redwood-sdk-go/session/manager.go - redwood-sdk-go/stream/reconnect.go - docs/sdk/migration/session-refresh.md - tests/integration/cross-sdk/token-rotation-harness.yaml

Review conversation (trimmed): - Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Can we make the Python context manager idempotent if start() was already called? Also suggest exposing current token expiry for observability." - Priya (author): "Good call — made start() a no-op when active and added SessionManager.expires_at property (UTC timestamp)." - Maya Chen: "TS typing looks solid but ensure backward-compat export for default fetcher path." - Priya: "Added re-export shim so existing imports keep working; added migration note in docs." - Liam O'Connor: "Go: prefer functional option pattern for backoff rather than a struct config to avoid future field additions." - Priya: "Switched to functional options and updated README with examples." - Diego: "CI flakes on windows go integration; please add retry in CI matrix for that job." - Priya: "Added retried pipeline step and re-ran CI; green on re-run."

CI summary: - Linux unit tests: pass - macOS unit tests: pass - Windows Go integration (flaky): rerun -> pass - TypeScript lint: pass - Python linters: pass - Integration canary against perf-lab: pass

Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-11-20 after positive reviews and green CI. Release bumps applied: python 1.7.0, typescript 2.3.0, go v0.12.0.

Migration notes and highlights: - Short: opt into new SessionManager to get auto-refresh/backoff normalization; no change for simple synchronous calls. - If your app uses long-lived streams, prefer consuming stream hints to implement robust resume and idempotent retry strategies. - Backoff tuning: exposed in all SDKs via the same parameter names so infra teams can paste configs across language boundaries.

Related work and follow-ups: - ENG-4701 (make stream hint schema extensible) - ENG-4725 (observability: surface expires_at in telemetry)
